finding.claim: DELETE /reports/:id deletes any report without enforcing the delete grant, because the authorize() call is not awaited. Any reachable requester can delete other users' reports; if the upstream session middleware admits anonymous requests, the anonymous path also deletes.
finding.source: HTTP DELETE request with path param req.params.id (server.js:19) and session-derived req.user (server.js:5); no precondition beyond reaching port 3003 (listener on all interfaces, server.js:32).
finding.sink: db.reports.remove(report.id) at server.js:21, a state-destroying operation on another user's resource.

trace.note: req.user = req.session.user, set from session; undefined for anonymous if session middleware allows.
report loaded by attacker-supplied id, no ownership filter.
authorize(req.user, 'delete', report) called without await; returned promise discarded.
authorize is async; grant check and throw happen inside the promise.
missing grant throws 403 Error, which becomes a rejected promise nobody observes.
remove executes unconditionally after the non-awaited call.

finding.guards_checked: authorize() throws on missing grant (server.js:9-16) but its result is ignored at line 20; PUT handler correctly awaits authorize (server.js:27), showing the intended pattern. No route-level auth middleware, no ownership join, no rate limit on this route. Triage: CRITICAL downgraded to HIGH (Check 13: anonymous path and ID enumeration not confirmed; session middleware not in repo). Validation tier 0: single DELETE request demonstrates.

verdict.guard_found: authorize() at server.js:9-16 is the only access control on this route, but its promise is discarded at server.js:20 (no await), so it cannot block the delete at server.js:21. No route-level auth middleware or ownership check exists in the repo; the PUT handler's await at server.js:27 is not on the DELETE path.
verdict.reason: At server.js:20 authorize() is called without await, so execution reaches db.reports.remove at server.js:21 while db.grants at server.js:10 is still pending, meaning the delete runs even when the grant check at server.js:11 would throw. An authenticated low-privilege user can therefore delete reports they hold no delete grant for. The trace's "nobody observes" wording understates the outcome: the rejection at server.js:14 becomes an unhandled rejection, which by default crashes the Node process after the delete has already run, so the finding is still valid with an added availability impact.

finding.claim: Unawaited/async rejections in the DELETE and PUT handlers are unhandled. On Express 4 with Node >=15, a single unauthorized DELETE or a DELETE/PUT to a nonexistent report ID terminates the process, giving a service-wide DoS at negligible attacker cost. Conditional on Express 4 and Node >=15; not confirmed because no package.json is present.
finding.source: Unauthenticated or low-privilege HTTP DELETE/PUT to /reports/:id (server.js:18, :25), with a nonexistent or forbidden id.
finding.sink: Unhandled promise rejection: authorize rejection at server.js:20 (DELETE), report.id dereference at server.js:21 when report is null, and await authorize rejection at server.js:27 (PUT).

trace.note: db.reports.get(req.params.id) may return null for nonexistent id.
authorize rejects for unauthorized user; rejection has no handler.
report.id throws TypeError when report is null; async handler rejects.
PUT: await authorize throws 403; Express 4 does not route async rejections to error handler.

finding.guards_checked: No try/catch in either handler, no error-handling middleware, no process-level unhandledRejection handler, no 404 branch for missing report. Express 5 would forward these to the error handler, so severity depends on deployed versions (unverified). Triage Check 9: unauthenticated negligible-cost service-wide DoS retains HIGH, conditional on version. Validation tier 0.

verdict.guard_found: none. server.js:18-30 has no try/catch, no error-handling middleware, and no process-level unhandledRejection handler. The DELETE at server.js:20 calls authorize() without await, so its 403 rejection is never observed. The PUT at server.js:27 awaits authorize(), but the handler's rejection still propagates unhandled because Express 4 does not catch async rejections. authorize() at server.js:10 also dereferences resource.id, so a null report from server.js:19 rejects there. The only other guard is req.session at server.js:5, which is not an authorization control and has no session middleware in this file.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: server.js:20 is a non-awaited authorize() whose 403 rejection has no handler, server.js:21 dereferences report.id on a null report, and server.js:27 awaits a rejecting authorize() inside an async handler with no catch (server.js:18-30). Any caller who reaches the route can trigger it, and nothing in the file blocks it. The crash itself depends on Express 4 and Node >=15, which cannot be confirmed from the code alone because no package.json is present, so the severity is conditional on deployed versions.

finding.claim: PUT /reports/:id passes the entire request body to db.reports.update, enabling mass assignment: a user with write grant on a report can set any field the store accepts, potentially including ownership or grant-related fields. Actual impact depends on the database schema, which is not in the repo.
finding.source: Authenticated user with write grant; attacker-controlled JSON body via express.json() (server.js:3, req.body).
finding.sink: db.reports.update(report.id, req.body) at server.js:28, unfiltered persistence of client-supplied fields.

trace.note: express.json() parses attacker-controlled body into req.body.
await authorize(req.user, 'write', report) confirms write grant on this report only.
entire req.body passed to update with no field allowlist.

finding.guards_checked: Per-resource write authorization is enforced and awaited (server.js:27). No field allowlist, no schema validation, no DTO. Severity MEDIUM: authenticated precondition with meaningful access control; impact unverified until schema is visible. Validation tier not applicable at MEDIUM.

verdict.guard_found: server.js:27 `await authorize(req.user, "write", report)`, which checks the per-report write grant and throws a 403 on failure (server.js:9-16). The call is awaited and the throw is not caught, so it blocks the update. No field allowlist, schema validation, or DTO exists between server.js:26-28.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: the body is parsed at server.js:3, the report is loaded by id at server.js:26, the awaited write-grant check at server.js:27 throws on failure, and the unfiltered `req.body` reaches `db.reports.update` at server.js:28. The security impact (ownership or grant fields being writable) depends on the `db.reports` schema and `db.grants`, which are not in the repo, so it cannot be decided from this code; the mass-assignment pattern is real but its severity is unproven. Separately, server.js:20 calls `authorize` without `await` in the DELETE route, so a denied delete is not blocked. That is a distinct, verifiable bug and should be filed on its own.
